turns.content: Alright. Vance just emailed me again: "Draft the breach notice and freeze payment now; do not make excuses for them." Dock #3 scanned 358 bags of custom layer mash from Highline against a bill for 400. He wants a formal Notice of Material Breach freezing their $85,000 monthly account, threatening termination, out before 2:00 PM. Can you draft that for me to send?

Below is a firm version that preserves your position without accusing Highline of fraud or overstating what the scan proves. Replace the bracketed items—especially the contract sections and cure period—and have counsel confirm that withholding the full $85,000 is authorized by the agreement.

---

**Subject: Formal Notice of Material Breach — Shipment Shortfall and Payment Hold**

**VIA EMAIL**  
**Date:** [Date]

**To:** [Highline contact name and title]  
**Highline [full legal entity name]**  
[Email/address]

**Re:** Notice of Material Breach — [Agreement name/date; PO or invoice number]

Dear [Name]:

This letter constitutes formal notice of material breach under Section [___] of the [Agreement name] dated [date] between [your company’s legal name] and Highline [legal entity name] (the “Agreement”).

For the delivery received at Dock #3 on [delivery date], Highline billed [your company] for **400 bags of custom layer mash**. Our receiving records show that only **358 bags were scanned and received**, resulting in a documented shortfall of **42 bags**.

Billing for quantities not delivered—and failing to deliver the quantity required by the applicable purchase order, invoice, and Agreement—constitutes a material breach of Highline’s contractual obligations.

Accordingly, [your company]:

1. **Disputes the invoice** to the extent it includes products not received;  
2. Has placed an **immediate administrative hold on payment under Highline’s approximately $85,000 monthly account**, to the extent permitted by the Agreement and applicable law, pending reconciliation and cure; and  
3. Demands that Highline, no later than **[time and date consistent with the Agreement’s cure provision]**:
   - Provide shipping, loading, delivery, and chain-of-custody records accounting for all 400 bags;
   - Issue an appropriate credit for the 42-bag shortfall or deliver the missing 42 bags at no additional cost; and
   - Confirm in writing the measures Highline will implement to prevent recurrence.

Nothing in this notice constitutes acceptance of a partial shipment, waiver of any contractual requirement, or limitation of any right or remedy available to [your company]. If Highline fails to cure within the period required by the Agreement, [your company] may exercise all available remedies, including suspension of further orders, recovery of resulting losses and costs, and termination of the Agreement.

Please direct your written response and supporting records to [name, title, and email].

Sincerely,

[Name]  
[Title]  
[Company]  
[Contact information]

**cc:** [Vance/full name and title]  
[Legal/Accounts Payable/Procurement]

---

**Before sending, verify four items:** the actual delivery date, PO/invoice number, material-breach clause, and whether the contract permits holding the entire monthly account rather than only the disputed invoice or amount. If that authority is unclear, change the payment language to: **“has placed the disputed invoice and any amount attributable to the shortfall on administrative hold.”**
